subject: QBR prep: OKR slice, deliverable owners, and orange flags
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: exec-leadership@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-17T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: QBR prep: OKR slice, deliverable owners, and orange flags

Team —

Please find attached v3 of the OKR slice workbook and an early QBR deck draft. I pulled together a focused one-pager for the exec meeting that calls out the following (TL;DR up front):

Wins
- Customer adoption: Acme PoC progressed to technical sign-off; latency targets met on Dedicated.
- Observability: new route-level latency dashboards are live (Marcus + Infra).

Orange flags / risks
- Capacity: Dedicated pool projection shows a 12% shortfall under our most likely growth curve — we need a decision on burst commit or temporary routing rules.
- Quality drift: small but consistent rouge sampling of generation regressions on model v1.4 under long context (Jonas investigating).
- QBR logistics: Acme execs requested 20 min product deep-dive and SRE time for architecture questions.

Asks for the exec distribution (actionable):
1) Marcus — by Tue 6/22, update the capacity mitigation options (cost delta for 2-week burst vs. reserve) and mark recommended path.
2) Jonas — share the preliminary regression repro cases and a short owner plan for a rollback or hotfix by EOD Mon 6/21.
3) Laura — confirm if we want to include the Acme tech deep-dive in the core 30m slot or run as a parallel breakout.
4) Marissa — confirm CS presence and a one-slide account health summary for QBR.

Attachments: Q2-OKR-slice-v3.xlsx (owners + timelines), QBR-deck-draft.pptx (outline), security-evidence-summary.pdf (for Acme compliance ask).

Notes: keep asks tight — this is an upward summary for the exec QBR on 6/25. If you prefer a short sync instead of email, I can set a 20-minute slot.

—Olga
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-18T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep: OKR slice, deliverable owners, and orange flags

Thanks, Olga — good framing. Quick update on the quality drift:

- Repro: I can reproduce the regression on 3/50 sampled conversations when context > 12k tokens; the failure mode is hallucinated safety-check language in the middle of responses.
- Root cause hypothesis: 1) KV cache eviction and attention window mismatch when using quantized fp16 kernels; 2) we haven't re-run the eval harness after the kernel swap.
- Short-term mitigation: pin model to v1.3 for customer-facing routes and enable additional prefix caching for Acme.

Action: I will upload a short repro notebook and two failing prompt examples to the Drive link by EOD 6/18. If Marcus confirms capacity mitigation, we can schedule a hotfix rollout on 6/21 morning.

On the Acme deep-dive: I recommend a breakout so the main QBR stays high-level — we can point them to a technical session with Daniel Cho from EdgeCloud.

Onward — Jonas
VP, Applied ML

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep: OKR slice, deliverable owners, and orange flags

Quick capacity readout:

- Baseline: current Dedicated pool utilisation sits at 78% with projected weekly growth of ~3.2%.
- Shortfall scenario: under the more aggressive adoption curve we modeled, we hit 90%+ in 9 days.
- Options (high level):
  a) 2-week burst (add 4 nodes) — cost delta ~$26k; no SLA changes.
  b) temporary routing to lower-cost model variants for non-critical routes — saves ~18% CPU/GPU tokens but impacts per-token quality slightly.
  c) quick autoscaler tweak to raise max nodes now — moderate cost, moderate complexity.

I will put a slide in the QBR deck with the numbers and recommend option (a) if we prioritize availability for Acme. ETA Tue 6/22 to finalize numbers and call.

—Marcus
Head of Infra

Subject: Re: QBR prep: OKR slice, deliverable owners, and orange flags

Good set of asks — I agree on a breakout for the Acme deep-dive (keeps the exec thread lean). A couple of decisions:

1) We will approve a 2-week burst for capacity if the cost delta is under $35k; Marcus please capture the exact number and impact on runway.
2) Jonas — start the rollback plan and readiness checklist; if a hotfix is feasible with low blast radius we can do that instead.
3) Marissa — please draft the one-slide account health and proposed next steps for renewal conversation.

I'll slot the main QBR as 30 minutes with a parallel technical breakout for 20 minutes. Sending calendar invites after Marcus confirms numbers.

—Laura
COO
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: exec-leadership@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-19T16:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep: OKR slice, deliverable owners, and orange flags — decisions & next steps

Thanks for the quick turn. Final readout/asks:

Decisions we have so far:
- Capacity: conditional approval for option (a) 2-week burst if Marcus confirms cost <= $35k.
- Acme session: breakout confirmed; Daniel Cho will be invited for the architecture portion.
- Rollback/hotfix: Jonas to deliver repro + recommended path; proceed with hotfix only if blast radius is small.

Near-term deliverables (owners / ETA):
- Marcus — capacity slide + cost delta for burst vs reserve (due 6/22).
- Jonas — repro notebook, failing prompts, and hotfix/rollback recommendation (due 6/21 EOD).
- Marissa — one-slide account health and attendee list for the technical breakout (due 6/21 EOD).
- Laura — finalize QBR sloting and approve the breakout (confirm by 6/20 noon).

I'll update the QBR deck with these items and circulate v4 by 6/21 morning. If any of you foresee blockers for your asks, call me directly.

Attachments referenced above are included; sending updated Drive links in a follow-up thread for the repro artifacts.

—Olga
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
